title: Dental work and saxophone players' mouths
summary: He describes bridges and caps costing thousands because years of pressure wear away gums and bone, citing Maynard Ferguson, Sonny Rollins and Coltrane.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well, saxophone player, trumpet player, they always have this problem with their teeth so I had some work done on my lower mouth and it cost me twelve hundred. It was a lower bridge I had put in and then, more recently, I had a partial bridge put up in my upper part of my mouth. That cost thirty-one hundred. But, you know, through the years your mouth, your gums and your bone structure...all that pressure through the years, you know, it wears away and the bone structure wears away and then your gums recede. So I had six caps put in in 1950. And my gums started receding and so they felt that that had to come out. And so I had this new work done, just recently, and it's a matter of adjustment. It takes a while but it's coming along, you know. Yeah. Maynard Ferguson has all of his teeth capped...the trumpet player that hits all the high notes. Yeah. And then I think Sonny Rollins has got a lot of work. And then I know that Coltrane had a lot of work done in his mouth. But this is important because
your playin' a horn and you have to have that firm foundation so that you can have confidence so you can play.
